note: No direction was dealt for this page: the owner supplied the comp (a reel of a reference site) and asked for it as close as possible. These rules are allowed because the comp does exactly this; each has its reason.

reasons.headline-lines: The comp's statements are a heavy caps title over two lines answered by one italic serif line (STOP LOSING / DAYS / to the airport.). Kept as the comp sets them.
reasons.mixed-font-headline: The caps grotesque + italic serif answer is the comp's typographic signature.
reasons.numbering: 01 / 04 is the fleet carousel's position, the only numbering on the page.
reasons.micro-label: Instrument labels (GS, HDG, ETE, ALTITUDE) and form field labels, as in the comp's HUD and booking card.
reasons.pinned-over-picture: The hero is a pinned film with words on it: the comp's whole first act. Text sits on scrims and changes with each chapter.
reasons.no-footage: The hero is the owner's film, drawn frame by frame on a canvas as the page scrolls.
reasons.edge-text: The fleet is a carousel: the next aircraft is cut by the screen edge on purpose, as in the comp.
reasons.side-scroll: On phones the fleet is a swipe row with snap points.
reasons.shadow: The framed prints in the light hall hang off the wall and cast a shadow on it, as in the comp.
reasons.gradient: The comp's gold actions are lit metal: a champagne-to-white gradient pill (ref_027, ref_029, ref_045). The impeccable finish review asked for it (FINISH: gold reads as metal, not yellow).
reasons.button-fx: Same pill: the comp gives it a top light and a soft glow.
reasons.palette-cream: The pale end of that metal gradient (#fbf3da) is the highlight on the gold, not a cream ground.
